key_insight: Simple-shear martensitic transformations enable elastic Landau states that assemble into closed, stress-free martensite islands within austenite.
engineering_relevance: The theory offers geometric guidance for designing self-accommodating transformation microstructures in shape-memory alloys, including through hierarchical twinning.
method: Identify two-parameter deformation families that permit closed, stress-free austenite–martensite interfaces.
Interpret simple shear and pure shear as cubic-to-monoclinic-II and cubic-to-orthorhombic transformations, respectively.
Assemble elastic Landau states into arbitrarily shaped martensitic islands.
evidence_signal: Predicted deformation gradients agree with gradients reconstructed from experimentally observed microstructures, although the abstract reports no quantitative agreement metrics.
watch_item: Geometric compatibility alone does not establish whether the proposed nuclei form under realistic energetic and kinetic constraints.
paper_title: Elastic Landau states as martensite nuclei in austenite
